check: whether the fault-matrix evidence can self-verify the way the S4 contract evidence does
why: The S4 evidence carries a logSha256 that I reproduced exactly, which makes it checkable without trusting the record. The fault matrix is cited for a much larger claim - 360 passing runs - so it was worth asking whether it has the same property.

whatItHas.exceptionRun: execution.json with sourceCommit 64b8947, runId, faultMode exception, repeats, points, passed and productionWiring
whatItHas.haltRun: execution.json with sourceCommit 3ff01db, the same shape
whatItHas.whatIsAbsent: Neither records a hash of its own results.json, so unlike the S4 evidence these cannot detect an edit to the results by themselves.

whyThatIsAcceptableHere: Both files are tracked by git, and git's blob hash is a content hash. Recomputed both with git hash-object and compared against the index: e8051efe... and 5a750fa4... match their recorded entries, and the working tree is clean. So an edit to either file would show as a modification rather than passing unnoticed.

theTwoEvidenceStyles.S4Contract: Self-contained: it hashes its own log so the record proves itself even outside version control, which matters because it was written to survive a build/ clean.
theTwoEvidenceStyles.FaultMatrix: Relies on version control for integrity, which is sufficient while the file stays committed - and it is, in commit 8cc63e8.
theTwoEvidenceStyles.neitherIsWrong: They differ because they answer different questions. One needed to outlive its build directory; the other needed to be a durable part of the repository.

whatWouldImproveIt: If the fault-matrix evidence ever needs to stand outside the repository, it would need the same kind of self-hash the S4 record has. Inside the repository that would duplicate what git already guarantees.
